digest.component_or_area: plan-review / code-review / completion gate verdict provenance
propositions: A signed gate verdict records only a resolved provider:model string, so a consumer cannot distinguish a Bedrock-backed verdict from an Ollama-backed one.
Add a sibling additive-only provider_provenance object (provider, model, endpoint_host, tier, capabilities) so older readers ignore it and no migration or compatibility gate is required.

The provenance record must be assembled in leaf module capabilities.py from primitives, reusing the caps record resolved once per run rather than recomputing it, and endpoint_host must use urlparse().hostname to strip credentials, never .netloc.

A negative-control test must assert no credential material from base_url or api_key appears anywhere in the persisted sidecar payload, and a legacy payload lacking provider_provenance must still load and verify.

Production wiring is incomplete: the gate verdict assembled by finalize_verdict never carries provider_provenance, so persisted payloads have the field absent despite passing unit tests on hand-built verdict dicts.

The same missing-provenance defect exists on the code-review and completion gates, and the fix is to thread the already-assembled record via the verify agent step's outputs rather than synthesizing a cfg-derived record where no model ran.
